contexts.text: When adulterers merely approach the heavenly Societies, they smell their own stink, and cast themselves down.

When (those in falsities) approach any heavenly Society, they smell rankly; and, when they smell it, they suppose it to flow forth from the heavenly Society, when yet it is from themselves; for a stink is not smelled except near its opposite. AC 7319.
When (their truths) fall off, they leave rank and stinking places from the falsities which exhale from the evils there.

When those (scortatory) places in Hell have been opened... such a stink has exhaled thence as to infest my stomach with heaviness; and, wonderful to say, these stinks are as delightful to them as ordure is to swine.
As such a delight... consumes itself, it becomes at last so rank to them, that they are at last kept living in a death-dealing stink...
